accepted.s: Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) is described as the world's largest publicly funded health assurance scheme. Its annual health cover is intended primarily for which purpose?
o: Preventive health check-ups for every citizen
accepted.x: AB-PMJAY provides health assurance of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise purpose linked with the scheme rather than its broad slogan.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to AB-PMJAY, consider the following statements:
1. The scheme was launched on 23 September 2018.
2. It was launched at Ranchi.
3. It provides a cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: AB-PMJAY was launched at Ranchi on 23 September 2018 and provides ₹5 lakh annual cover per family.
accepted.tq: Combine a date, place and numerical figure in one statement set.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The original beneficiary base of AB-PMJAY was designed to cover approximately:
accepted.x: The scheme was based on approximately 12 crore families, covering around 55 crore people, corresponding broadly to the bottom 40 percent of the population.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired family and population figures together.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Beneficiaries of AB-PMJAY were primarily identified using which basis?
accepted.x: The beneficiary base was identified using deprivation criteria from the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011. States may widen the base at their own cost.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the identification database from other commonly used databases.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of AB-PMJAY?
o: A mandatory cap on family size
Coverage of pre-existing diseases from the first day
accepted.x: AB-PMJAY has no cap on family size or age. It is cashless, paperless, portable nationwide and covers pre-existing diseases from day one.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed feature by checking the word that contradicts the scheme design.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the beneficiary profile and coverage under AB-PMJAY is correct?
o: Women are restricted to less than 10% of admissions.
Childhood cancer is excluded from the scheme.
Women account for approximately 49% of cards and 48% of admissions.
Pre-existing diseases are covered only after a waiting period.
accepted.x: Childhood cancer is covered, pre-existing diseases are covered from day one, and women hold approximately 49% of cards and account for about 48% of admissions.
accepted.tq: Use the precise percentage pair to separate a correct profile statement from exclusions.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the funding pattern of AB-PMJAY?
o: Centre-State 50:50 in all States and 100% State funding in Union Territories
Centre-State 60:40; 90:10 in North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Jammu and Kashmir; 100% Centre funding in Union Territories without legislature
100% Central funding in every State and Union Territory
accepted.x: The normal Centre-State ratio is 60:40, changing to 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Jammu and Kashmir; Union Territories without legislatures receive 100% Central funding.
accepted.tq: Compare the normal, special-region and Union Territory funding ratios.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ayushman Vay Vandana card under AB-PMJAY is meant for:
o: Children below 10 years from SECC households
Only women aged 70 years and above
All persons aged 60 years and above subject to an income ceiling
All persons aged 70 years and above irrespective of income
accepted.x: All senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for the Ayushman Vay Vandana card irrespective of income.
accepted.tq: Test the age threshold together with the important income-related exception.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As on 28 October 2025, which combination correctly describes the scale of AB-PMJAY?
o: 30 crore cards, 5 crore admissions worth ₹50,000 crore, and 10,000 hospitals
86.51 crore cards, 10.3 crore admissions worth ₹1.49 lakh crore, and 33,000 hospitals
55 crore cards, 12 crore admissions worth ₹2 lakh crore, and 50,000 hospitals
42 crore-plus cards, 10.3 crore admissions worth ₹1.49 lakh crore, and more than 33,000 hospitals
accepted.x: By 28 October 2025, more than 42 crore cards had been issued, with 10.3 crore admissions worth ₹1.49 lakh crore across more than 33,000 hospitals.
accepted.tq: Match the date with the complete three-part scale figure.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ayushman Arogya Mandir, formerly known as Health and Wellness Centres, primarily provides:
o: Comprehensive primary care through about 1.5 lakh centres, with primary care addressing 80–90% of needs
accepted.x: Ayushman Arogya Mandir is the primary-care umbrella under Ayushman Bharat. The original target was about 1.5 lakh centres, and primary care is stated to meet 80–90% of needs.
accepted.tq: Link the institutional name with its level and estimated coverage of health needs.
accepted.sec: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover, beneficiaries, features, senior citizens  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: ABDM — District critical-care blocks as its principal aim
accepted.x: PM-ABHIM aims to create pandemic-ready health infrastructure, whereas ABDM seeks an interoperable digital health ecosystem.
accepted.tq: Separate the physical-health-infrastructure mission from the digital-health mission.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. PM-ABHIM was launched in October 2021 at Varanasi.
2. ABDM was launched in September 2021.
3. ABDM had earlier been announced as the National Digital Health Mission on 15 August 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: PM-ABHIM was launched at Varanasi in October 2021. ABDM was launched in September 2021 and had been announced as NDHM on 15 August 2020.
accepted.tq: Check the two launch dates along with the earlier name and announcement date.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the principal components of PM-ABHIM?
accepted.x: District critical-care blocks, Integrated Public Health Laboratories, BSL-3 laboratories and surveillance are associated with PM-ABHIM. The four-registry architecture belongs to ABDM.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-component trap to distinguish the two Ayushman Bharat missions.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PM-ABHIM involves an expenditure of approximately:
accepted.x: The expenditure indicated for PM-ABHIM is ₹64,180 crore over six years.
accepted.tq: Recall the scheme's expenditure and implementation period as a pair.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the institutional character of PM-ABHIM and ABDM?
o: PM-ABHIM is a State Sector Scheme and ABDM is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
PM-ABHIM is a CSS with central components, while ABDM is a Central Sector initiative run by the National Health Authority.
Both are Central Sector Schemes run by the National Health Authority.
Both are implemented exclusively by State health departments.
accepted.x: PM-ABHIM has the character of a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with central components. ABDM is a Central Sector initiative run by the National Health Authority.
accepted.tq: Compare scheme type and implementing authority rather than only the stated objectives.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The four principal registries associated with ABDM are:
o: Aadhaar, PAN, HPR and GST Registry
HPR, NHA, PM-JAY and Drug Registry
ABHA, HPR, HFR and Drug Registry
ABHA, SECC, HFR and Census Registry
accepted.x: The four ABDM registries are ABHA, Healthcare Professionals Registry, Health Facilities Registry and the Drug Registry.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact members of a named four-item list.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to ABHA, consider the following statements:
1. It is a 14-digit health ID.
2. It links lifelong health records.
3. Participation is voluntary and consent-based.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: ABHA is a 14-digit health ID designed to link lifelong records, and participation is voluntary and based on consent.
accepted.tq: Combine the identifier's format, function and consent condition.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about ABDM is correct?
o: ABHA is an eight-digit insurance claim number without record-linking capacity.
The National Medical Commission directed all medical colleges to link records with ABHA in March 2026.
ABDM is operated by the World Bank.
ABHA participation is compulsory for every citizen.
accepted.x: In March 2026, the National Medical Commission directed all medical colleges to link records with ABHA. Participation in ABHA remains voluntary and consent-based.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct authority and action in a policy-direction question.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A World Bank loan of US$1 billion for PM-ABHIM was reported in:
accepted.x: The World Bank loan of US$1 billion for PM-ABHIM was reported in July 2022.
accepted.tq: Associate the financial amount with its specific month and year.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the Andhra Pradesh-related digital health developments mentioned?
o: Sanjeevani is limited to private hospitals and excludes PHCs.
Andhra Pradesh generated 5.04 crore ABHA accounts, and its Sanjeevani programme began in August 2026.
Andhra Pradesh generated 50.4 lakh ABHA accounts, and Sanjeevani began in August 2020.
Private medical colleges in Andhra Pradesh were prohibited from using ABHA.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh had generated 5.04 crore ABHA accounts. Its Sanjeevani digital health programme began in August 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical scale and launch month to reject altered AP-specific claims.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Sanjeevani in Andhra Pradesh is intended to integrate which of the following?
1. PHCs
2. e-Aushadhi
3. 108 and 104 services
4. Telemedicine and AI
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Sanjeevani is intended to create a health profile and ABHA for every citizen while integrating PHCs, e-Aushadhi, 108, 104, telemedicine and AI.
accepted.tq: Test completeness of a multi-component digital-health integration list.
accepted.sec: PM-ABHIM and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - launch, ABHA, participation, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the latest figures cited, government health expenditure was approximately what percentage of GDP, against the NHP 2017 target?
accepted.x: Government health expenditure was 1.43% of GDP, while the National Health Policy 2017 target is 2.5% of GDP.
accepted.tq: Keep the actual value and policy target in the correct order.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure on health - National Health Accounts, OOPE, NHP 2017  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Household out-of-pocket expenditure constituted what share of total health expenditure in 2022–23 according to the cited figures?
accepted.x: Household out-of-pocket expenditure constituted 43.4% of total health expenditure in 2022–23.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the OOPE share from other health-sector percentages.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure on health - National Health Accounts, OOPE, NHP 2017  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which change in the health sector's share of government spending was reported between 2021–22 and 2022–23?
accepted.x: The health share of government spending declined from 6.12% in 2021–22 to 4.89% in 2022–23.
accepted.tq: Read the direction of change before comparing the two percentages.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure on health - National Health Accounts, OOPE, NHP 2017  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the reported health expenditure pattern is correct?
o: Medicines accounted for approximately 21% of current health expenditure.
Private childbirth OOPE was ₹2,299, compared with ₹37,630 in the public sector.
Private providers supplied less than 10% of inpatient care.
The private sector supplied approximately 20% of outpatient care.
accepted.x: Medicines accounted for approximately 21% of current health expenditure. The reported childbirth OOPE was ₹37,630 in private care and ₹2,299 in public care; private providers supplied over 60% of inpatient and about 70% of outpatient care.
accepted.tq: Select the exact percentage while using reversed comparison figures as traps.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure on health - National Health Accounts, OOPE, NHP 2017  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term “missing middle” in Indian health financing refers to:
o: Urban households receiving both public and private health insurance
People fully covered by government subsidies but unable to access public hospitals
Only informal workers excluded from employment insurance
More than 40 crore people outside full subsidy coverage who cannot afford private care
accepted.x: The missing middle consists of more than 40 crore Indians who are outside full subsidy coverage but cannot afford private healthcare.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to a population and coverage situation.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure on health - National Health Accounts, OOPE, NHP 2017  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective associated with the National Health Policy 2017?
o: Restricting public health services exclusively to tertiary hospitals
Shifting emphasis from curative care to preventive and primary care
Raising public health spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2025
accepted.x: NHP 2017 envisaged higher public health spending, a shift toward preventive and primary care, and universal health coverage. It did not seek to restrict services to tertiary hospitals.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated policy direction.
accepted.sec: Public expenditure on health - National Health Accounts, OOPE, NHP 2017  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 was approved by the Union Cabinet on:
accepted.x: NEP 2020 was approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 July 2020.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact approval date rather than the policy-announcement date.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: NEP 2020 was drafted by a committee chaired by:
o: The Chairman of the National Medical Commission
accepted.x: The committee that drafted NEP 2020 was chaired by Dr K. Kasturirangan.
accepted.tq: Match the policy with its drafting committee chairperson.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The school education structure proposed under NEP 2020 is:
accepted.x: NEP 2020 proposes the 5+3+3+4 structure covering ages 3–8, 8–11, 11–14 and 14–18 respectively.
accepted.tq: Recall the official structural sequence and its four age bands.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the stages of the NEP 2020 school structure with their age groups?
1. Foundational stage — 3–8 years
2. Preparatory stage — 8–11 years
3. Middle stage — 11–14 years
4. Secondary stage — 14–18 years
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The four stages correspond respectively to 3–8, 8–11, 11–14 and 14–18 years.
accepted.tq: Verify every stage-age pairing instead of relying only on the 5+3+3+4 sequence.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India is required under the cited NEP-related target to raise Expected Years of Schooling to:
accepted.x: The cited target is to raise Expected Years of Schooling to 15 years.
accepted.tq: Recall the single quantitative schooling-outcome target.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following targets is correctly associated with NEP 2020?
o: 50% GER in higher education by 2035 and 100% GER from pre-school to secondary level by 2030
Universal higher education by 2030 without a school GER target
100% GER in higher education by 2035 and 50% GER in school education by 2030
50% GER in higher education by 2025 and public education spending of 2.5% of GDP
accepted.x: NEP 2020 targets 50% gross enrolment ratio in higher education by 2035 and 100% GER from pre-school to secondary level by 2030.
accepted.tq: Keep the two GER targets linked to their correct education levels and years.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The public education expenditure target associated with NEP 2020 is:
accepted.x: NEP 2020 envisages public education spending of 6% of GDP.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the education-spending target from the health-spending target.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Scheme)
A. ULLAS
B. DIKSHA
C. Samagra Shiksha
D. NIPUN Bharat

List-II (Purpose)
1. Foundational literacy and numeracy
2. Digital infrastructure for knowledge sharing and e-content
3. Adult literacy
4. Integrated school education

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: ULLAS concerns adult literacy; DIKSHA is the digital infrastructure and e-content platform; Samagra Shiksha integrates school education; NIPUN Bharat focuses on foundational literacy and numeracy.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched scheme purposes.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
1. PM-SHRI — Model schools
2. PARAKH — Assessment regulator
3. Vidya Pravesh — School readiness
4. PM POSHAN — Digital learning platform
accepted.x: PM POSHAN is associated with school meals, not a digital learning platform. PM-SHRI, PARAKH and Vidya Pravesh are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the single swapped purpose in a closely related scheme list.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Curriculum Frameworks for the Foundational Stage (2022) and School Education (2023) were developed by:
accepted.x: Both the NCF for Foundational Stage (2022) and the NCF for School Education (2023) were developed by NCERT.
accepted.tq: Match both named curriculum frameworks with their institutional source.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the scale of school education cited for India?
o: 14.71 lakh schools, 24.69 crore students, all of them government schools, and around 50% aged 3–18
24.69 lakh schools, 14.71 crore students, about 27% government schools, and around 69% aged 3–18
14.71 lakh schools, 24.69 crore students, about 69% government schools, and around 27% of the population aged 3–18
10.47 lakh schools, 14.69 crore students, about 50% government schools, and around 17% aged 3–18
accepted.x: The cited scale is 14.71 lakh schools and 24.69 crore students; government schools constitute about 69%, and approximately 27% of the population is aged 3–18.
accepted.tq: Match all four scale indicators without reversing schools, students or percentages.
accepted.sec: NEP 2020 - drafting committee, structure, GER, linked schemes, NCF  [APPSC]
